episode_title: Winning B2B Attention in the Age of AI Content | In Conversation with Josh Ritchie

real_qa.q: How did Column 5 transition from a clothing retail business to becoming a B2B content agency?
real_qa.r: Josh Ritchie, Ross, and Jason started by creating a blog focused on apparel brands to drive traffic to their clothing store and online business. People began noticing their content quality and asking them to create content as a paid service. Their first paid gig was a $75 post for Art of Manliness, split three ways. After word of mouth, they were approached by Mint.com, which became a watershed moment with their first real big budget project, eventually leading them to realize there was more money in content creation than their retail businesses.

real_qa.q: What is the biggest shift in B2B marketing strategy between Google search optimization and AI-powered search results?
real_qa.r: The script has been completely flipped from prioritizing top-of-funnel, high-volume content to prioritizing bottom-of-funnel and mid-funnel content. Google changed its search algorithm at the same time GPT and Anthropic rolled out, causing both search results and buyer behavior to shift dramatically. What worked for SEO seven years ago is different than what's working now, and good SEO is now important for good AEO (AI Engine Optimization).
real_qa.requete: B2B marketing SEO vs AEO algorithm changes

real_qa.q: How has buyer behavior changed regarding where B2B professionals search for solutions?
real_qa.r: People are no longer going to Google as much to search for solutions like 'what's a good creative agency for B2B SaaS'. Instead, they are going to AI tools like ChatGPT or Claude asking 'who should I talk to'. The shift has been rapid and mainstream—even non-tech professionals are now using AI search instead of Google. At Focus Lab, half of their leads now come from AI search, half from traditional sources.
real_qa.requete: buyer behavior ChatGPT Google search shift

real_qa.q: What is Column 5's approach to using AI tools in client work while maintaining ethical transparency?
real_qa.r: Column 5 published an AI code of ethics addressing transparency and proactively communicating how they use AI. They use AI for efficiency tasks like data entry, data cleanup, and creating brand assets at different dimensions, but explicitly do not use it for creative work or writing blog posts for clients. Their mentality is to own how AI is used, decide what they want and don't want to use it for, and make that accessible to clients and prospects.
real_qa.requete: Column 5 AI ethics code of conduct

real_qa.q: Why does being AI-forward become a competitive requirement for B2B agencies even when AI adoption may not be core to their value proposition?
real_qa.r: Many companies, whether brand teams or marketing teams, are being issued mandates from the board to work with AI-forward agencies. This is similar to how the narrative was 'cloud computing company' a decade ago—it eventually becomes part of the background infrastructure rather than a differentiating message. The hive mind in tech currently demands AI-forward positioning, but this will likely subside in one to two years when it becomes an assumed baseline.
real_qa.requete: AI forward agency mandate tech industry trend

real_qa.q: How should B2B brands balance messaging about AI capabilities without over-indexing or under-indexing on the feature?
real_qa.r: The key is focusing on benefits versus features rather than trivializing or oversimplifying the work. Some companies genuinely need AI to be their core message due to board mandates or actual relevance, while others should treat it as part of the infrastructure without making it the primary message. For companies trying to transform their narrative to appear more AI-forward, the balance requires careful positioning to avoid both minimizing AI's relevance and making it seem like a gimmick.
real_qa.requete: AI messaging brand positioning benefits features

guest.bio_context: Josh Ritchie co-founded Column 5 in 2009 alongside Ross and Jason. He initially worked as creative director and CEO before transitioning to lead sales, business development and marketing efforts. The agency has been focused on helping B2B SaaS companies refine and tell their story at scale for over 15 years, working with clients including Databricks and JP Morgan.
